summary: Frontend-only test of iteration_25 wake-word feature. All 11 requested test cases pass. Toggle button state changes, localStorage persistence (sertex_wake_settings_v1), event-driven wake-triggered flow (with & without tail), regressions (send flow, alarm tab, voice-auto-hint, DUR TTS button surface), and HUD layout (height=290 >= 280) all verified. No JS console errors during full flow.

issues: Enabled state jumps directly from disabled (muted) to emerald/active because Chromium supports webkitSpeechRecognition and listener.start() succeeds immediately — the intermediate yellow (enabled-but-not-active) state is hard to observe in Playwright. Not a bug, but worth noting: in production Firefox/mobile browsers the emerald state would never appear because SR isn't supported; the code correctly falls back to an error toast + disables the setting. Verified this fallback works.

critical_code_review_comments: wakeWord.js: rec.onend restart on 'aborted' error path could tight-loop if permission is denied silently. The 'not-allowed' branch correctly stops, but if start() throws synchronously (e.g. AbortError) inside setTimeout callback of onend, the error is swallowed. Consider tracking a failure counter and giving up after N restarts.

SertexMain.jsx handleSend: resumeWakeListener() is called inside try, catch and finally-equivalent paths — good. But wakePendingResumeRef is only set inside the wake onWake callback; if a wake-triggered command times out or errors before handleSend runs, the ref may stay true and cause an unwanted resume on the next manual send. Consider clearing the ref on wakeEnabled=false and on any early return in handleSend.

HUDOverlay.jsx line 151: The text 'SERTEX'İ DİNLE' repeats identically in enabled-non-active and disabled states — only color changes. For accessibility, consider adding an aria-pressed attribute or distinct sr-only text so screen readers can convey state.

InputBar.jsx line 38-55: The useEffect for wake event listener depends on [listening, transcribing, disabled] — every time these change the listener is torn down and re-added. That's fine for a lightweight window listener, but it means a wake event that fires DURING a state transition could be missed. Consider using refs for the guards instead of dependency array.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Wake-word feature is fully functional. localStorage key: sertex_wake_settings_v1 with { enabled: bool }. Custom events: sertex:wake-triggered (from wakeWord listener; detail.tail is optional command text) and sertex:wake-settings-changed (fires on toggle). InputBar listens for wake-triggered and auto-calls startListening(); if detail.tail is non-empty it seeds the chat-input state. Testing tip: dispatch the custom event via page.evaluate to bypass real STT audio pipeline — that's what these tests do. Grant ['microphone'] permission on the page origin so getUserMedia + SpeechRecognition succeed in Chromium. Known flakiness: clicking wake-word-toggle immediately after closing the Settings modal via Escape may miss the first click due to modal unmount timing — wait ~500ms or click Settings' close button explicitly. Also note: the enabled-but-not-active (yellow) visual state is essentially unobservable in Chromium because SR.start() succeeds synchronously — you'll see either muted (disabled) or emerald (enabled+active).
